history.summary: A prominent Siddha Peeth dedicated to Goddess Bagalamukhi, one of the ten Mahavidyas of Tantric Shaktism, revered as Pitambara (clothed in yellow) for stambhan shakti - paralyzing enemies, victory in legal disputes and protection from evil. Legend holds she emerged from the Haridra Sarovar to calm a cosmic storm at Vishnu's request; the Pandavas are said to have built the temple overnight during their exile, and Rama is said to have worshipped here before facing Ravana. It is counted among the three most significant Baglamukhi shrines in India (with Datia and Nalkheda in Madhya Pradesh). No historically verified construction date or dynasty; a '~1000 years old' claim appears in travel sources without evidence. CORRECTION: CSV town 'Palampur' is WRONG; the temple is at Bankhandi (PIN 177114), near Dehra in Kangra district on the Chandigarh-Dharamshala highway (NH-503), ~60+ km from Palampur. Coordinates are Bankhandi village-level (OSM/mapcarta 31.95992, 76.20304) - approximate, verify at POI level. Navratri listed as the standard Devi-temple festival; temple-specific festival calendar not documented in consulted sources (verify).

name: Shri Baglamukhi Mata Temple
town_description: Bankhandi (PIN 177114) is a village in Dehra tehsil of Kangra district on the Chandigarh-Dharamshala highway (NH-503), ~30-40 km from Kangra town. The Baglamukhi temple makes it a major Shakti pilgrimage destination.

travel.railway: Kangra Mandir station, ~40 km (per district tourism site)
travel.road: On NH-503 (Chandigarh-Dharamshala highway), 30-40 km from Kangra town; buses and taxis from Kangra, Dharamshala and Pathankot

visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning aarti ~5:00 AM; darshan from 6:00 AM; shayan aarti ~8:00 PM (per yatradham blog - verify locally)
